overview: Vista Group is a New Zealand-headquartered software company that provides the mission-critical technology backbone for the global cinema and film distribution industry, spanning box-office/ticketing and cinema management (Vista Cinema, Vista Cloud, Veezi), marketing and loyalty data analytics (Movio), and box-office reporting/distribution analytics (Numero, Maccs, Movio Research, Powster, Flicks). Founded in 1996 and now in its fourth decade, Vista holds an estimated 46-48% enterprise market share of the global cinema exhibition market (ex-China, India, Russia), operating across six continents and serving marquee exhibitors including AMC/ODEON, Kinepolis, Cineplex, Cinepolis, Cineworld and Village Cinemas. The company is mid-transition from legacy on-premise/license software to a cloud/SaaS and payments platform (Vista Cloud, Vista Payments), targeting an ARR exit-rate aspiration of $315m by 2030.

business_model.summary: Vista monetizes cinema and film-distribution clients through a mix of legacy on-premise licenses/maintenance (declining), growing SaaS/cloud subscriptions (Vista Cloud, Veezi, Movio EQ) and usage/GTV-linked revenue (payments, box-office-linked data products). ~90% of revenue is now classified as Recurring Revenue, with SaaS Revenue (cloud-native, usage/subscription based) the fastest-growing component. Two reporting segments: Cinema (~80% of FY25 revenue) covering cinema management/ticketing/marketing software, and Film (~20%) covering studio/distributor tools (Maccs, Numero, Movio Research, Powster, Flicks).

revenue_streams.name: Cinema segment (Vista Cloud, Vista Classic, Veezi, Movio EQ)
Film segment (Maccs, Numero, Movio Research, Powster, Flicks)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise — global cinema exhibitors (from large multinational circuits like AMC/ODEON and Kinepolis down to independent single-site cinemas) and film studios/distributors
business_model.geographic_mix: Global footprint across six continents; historically weighted to North America and EMEA cinema circuits with growing Latin America (Cinepolis, Cinemex) and Asia-Pacific presence; NZ-domiciled reporting currency (NZD) with revenue predominantly earned in USD, EUR and other foreign currencies, creating translation exposure

main_competitors: In-house/proprietary systems of very large exhibitors (e.g., AMC, Cinemark)
Regional cinema POS/ticketing vendors (e.g., Agile Ticketing, Filmbank/WhatsOnCinema in UK, Ymagis/CJ 4DPlex-related regional tools)
Comscore / Gower Street Analytics (box-office data and analytics)
Legacy on-premise software vendors being displaced by cloud transition
competitive_position.market_position: Global category leader — management estimates ~46-48% enterprise market share of the world cinema exhibition market (screens 20+, excluding China, India and Russia), with limited direct competition at enterprise scale; considered the de facto 'operating system' for the film distribution-to-exhibition value chain

moat_factors.description: Vista is the authoritative system of record for box-office/revenue-share reporting between exhibitors and studios; downtime stops revenue generation, and workflows (ticketing, scheduling, F&B, marketing, payments) are deeply interwoven, making rip-and-replace costly and risky
Requires market-specific certified box-office reporting connections, localisation/homologation, SOC2/PCI/GDPR compliance built over 30 years — high cost of entry for new entrants

Aggregated global cinema/moviegoer data (100m+ moviegoers, 750m+ behavioural records via Movio) underpins AI-driven products (CLV/churn models, box-office forecasting) that are difficult to replicate without comparable scale

moat_factors.factor: Dominant market share in a niche vertical
moat_factors.description: ~46-48% enterprise share outside China/India/Russia limits the number of credible full-stack competitors

moat_factors.factor: Usage/outcome-based pricing resistant to seat erosion
moat_factors.description: Large components of revenue link to client GTV/usage rather than per-seat software licenses, and management estimates Vista's cost is under 1% of client revenue, reducing price sensitivity

weaknesses: Small-cap/micro-cap scale relative to global software peers limits R&D budget and negotiating leverage with major exhibitor groups
Revenue and profitability remain tied to cinema industry health, box-office slate strength and exhibitor capex appetite
Cloud/SaaS transition is a multi-year, capital- and cost-intensive migration (only 35% of sites transitioned to Vista Cloud as of FY25) with execution risk and near-term margin drag
History of shareholder activism/governance friction (2024-2025 Potentia/Admetus boardroom dispute) created distraction and uncertainty
Long-tenured co-founder director (Murray Holdaway, non-independent, ~22 years on board, ~2.4% shareholder) raises governance concentration questions even as the rest of the board is independent

growth_drivers: Vista Cloud migration — 35% of cinema sites transitioned to cloud at FY25 (up from ~16-19% base), with a large signed pipeline (ODEON/AMC 295 additional sites by 2027, Kinepolis 109 sites, Cinepolis Mexico 504 sites/6-year deal, Cineworld UK 88 sites, Cinemex return) expected to lift SaaS revenue mix and margins
Vista Payments — newly launched embedded payments product; ARR surpassed $2m with 11 clients live by H1-2026, targeting $15m+ ARR aspiration and ~US$22b implied gross transaction value by 2030

AI-enabled product roadmap — CLV/churn prediction, box-office/assisted-scheduling forecasting, moviegoer personas/segmentation, and agentic commerce (discovery/transactions) layered on proprietary 30-year data set, positioned as an AI beneficiary rather than a disruption target
Adjacent-market expansion — Family Entertainment Centres (FECs) and film distribution workflows identified as identified adjacencies to extend total addressable market beyond core cinema exhibition
Operating leverage from the cloud transition — EBITDA margin guided to expand from 17.2% (FY25) to 18-20% (FY26 guidance) as onboarding costs are recovered and scale benefits accrue

Secular box-office recovery — global box office rose 12% YoY to US$33.6bn in 2025, with 2026 domestic box office forecast up ~14% on a stronger film slate (Star Wars, Avengers, Dune, Toy Story, Mission-critical tentpoles), directly benefiting Vista's usage/GTV-linked revenue

business.risk: Cinema industry cyclicality and content-slate dependency
business.description: Vista's usage/GTV-linked revenue and its exhibitor clients' capex/willingness to invest are sensitive to box-office strength, which depends on the annual film slate; a weak slate year (as seen intermittently post-COVID and during the 2023 writers'/actors' strikes) directly pressures revenue and client budgets
Long-run secular risk that streaming reduces theatrical attendance frequency, even though recent data show resilience and growing Gen Z engagement

A small number of marquee multinational exhibitors (AMC/ODEON, Kinepolis, Cineworld, Cinepolis) represent large blocks of sites; loss or renegotiation of a major account could be material (Cinemex's prior departure and 2026 return illustrates this volatility)

business.risk: Execution risk in the cloud migration
business.description: Only 35% of sites transitioned to Vista Cloud as of FY25; management explicitly flags client demand outpacing delivery capacity, requiring continued hiring/investment, with incremental costs not expected to be fully recovered through higher free cash flow until 'before the end of 2030'

Generic AI tools could in theory lower barriers for new entrants in scheduling, marketing or data analytics, though Vista argues its workflow-embedded, regulated, proprietary data moat is AI-resistant

financial.description: NZD reporting currency against predominantly USD/EUR-denominated client revenue creates translation volatility; EBITDA margin is reported both as-stated and 'adjusted for exchange' in guidance and LTI targets

financial.risk: Swing to net debt during investment phase
financial.description: Net cash of $0.7m at FY25 flipped to net debt of ~$5.8m at H1-2026 as the company continues to invest ~$8.5m incremental in delivery/technology capacity to accelerate cloud onboarding

financial.risk: Thin/negative net profit and negative net tangible assets
financial.description: FY25 NPAT was only $2.6m on $164.3m revenue; H1-2026 posted a net loss of $1.5m (widened from $1.2m in H1-2025); net tangible assets per share were negative $0.031 at H1-2026 (vs negative $0.017 a year earlier), reflecting an intangible-heavy balance sheet

financial.risk: No dividend and no credit rating
financial.description: Vista adopted a refreshed dividend policy after reaching free-cash-flow positivity in H2-2024 but declared no dividend for FY2025, prioritising reinvestment in the cloud transition

regulatory.description: Operates in regulated markets handling personal/identifiable moviegoer data (GDPR and equivalent regimes across dozens of countries); Vista disclosed one notifiable privacy breach (employee data) during FY2025
Market-specific certified box-office reporting and local homologation requirements must be maintained across many jurisdictions as Vista expands geographically

macro.description: Cinema attendance and exhibitor capex are consumer discretionary and macro-cyclical; a recession or cost-of-living squeeze could reduce moviegoing frequency and delay client technology spend

Management explicitly cited 'challenging year for shareholder returns amid global volatility in software company valuations' in the FY25 Chair's letter; VGL's share price fell from a 52-week high of NZ$3.54 to a low of NZ$1.56 before partially recovering, reflecting broader small-cap software multiple compression

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global theatrical box office grew 12% YoY to US$33.6bn in 2025 and is forecast to grow further in 2026 (Gower Street projects ~14% domestic growth) on a stronger content slate; industry commentary (Cinema United/NATO) points to resilient, even strengthening, moviegoing engagement among younger (Gen Z) audiences and continued investment by exhibitors in premium formats, F&B and family entertainment centre diversification
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — Vista's usage/GTV-linked and license revenue correlates with cinema attendance and the annual film slate (evidenced by the 2023 writers'/actors' strike hit to Powster and broader industry revenue), though the growing recurring/subscription (SaaS) mix and multi-year enterprise contracts are dampening cyclicality over time
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect exposure — as a small-cap growth/software name reliant on continued capital investment (Vista Cloud build-out) and currently running near break-even/net debt, higher rates raise the cost of any external financing and pressure growth-stock valuation multiples
key_input_costs: Software engineering/technology talent (Vista Cloud and AI development)

recent_developments.event: H1-2026 results: revenue $86.3m (+12.1% YoY), EBITDA $12.4m (+24%, 13.8% FX-adjusted margin), ARR $170.1m (+17% YoY), SaaS revenue $43.5m (+38%), Vista Payments ARR surpassed $2m with 11 clients live, but net loss widened to $1.5m (from $1.2m in H1-2025) and balance sheet swung to ~$5.8m net debt from $0.7m net cash at FY25; no interim dividend declared
FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $179m-$184m (from $176m-$182m); EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 18%-20%; management guided to free-cash-flow neutrality in H2-2026

Major new Vista Cloud client wins signed/expanded: Cinepolis Mexico (6-year deal, 504 sites/4,100+ screens), Cineworld/Regal UK (88 sites, ~950 screens, Digital Enablement), Cinemex returned to Vista Group (5-year deal, 300+ net new sites) and Cineplexx; Contracted Enterprise Market Share rose from 46% to 48%
Forsyth Barr raised its price target on VGL by 12% to NZ$3.28/share following strong trading updates

FY2025 annual results: record revenue $164.3m (+10%), recurring revenue $147.2m (+9%), SaaS revenue $69.7m (+25%), ARR $163.0m (+12%), EBITDA $28.2m (+31%, 17.2% margin, up from 14.4%), return to net profit of $2.6m (from a $0.6m loss in FY24), operating cash flow $27.8m (+65%); FY2026 initial guidance issued: revenue $176m-$182m, EBITDA margin 18%-20%

Admetus Capital (Potentia), which had built a 19.9% stake in May 2024 and requisitioned a special meeting in 2024 seeking to remove Chair Susan Peterson and director Kirk Senior in favour of its own nominees (a campaign it later withdrew after failing to secure majority shareholder support), fully exited its entire shareholding (~45.7m shares, ~19.8%) via a block trade at NZ$3.00/share (a ~5% discount), ending a 15-month activist involvement; the associated New Shareholder Committee was disestablished
Long-serving director Kirk Senior (11 years, former Village Cinemas CEO and former Vista Executive Chair) retired from the Board; a director succession process was reactivated
Vista Cloud and movieXchange achieved SOC 2 Type 2 certification, reinforcing security/compliance credentials for enterprise clients
Vista Payments launched commercially with initial pilot clients live and transacting, marking entry into embedded payments as a new high-margin recurring revenue stream

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 results (3 August 2026), updating FY2025 Annual Report guidance (26 February 2026)

items.notes: Raised from initial FY2026 guidance of $176m-$182m given at FY2025 results, following 12.1% H1 revenue growth and accelerating Vista Cloud/Vista Payments onboarding
Unchanged from initial guidance; up from 17.2% actual in FY2025; H1-2026 FX-adjusted margin of 13.8% (+1.9pts YoY) implies typical second-half weighting
Balance sheet swung to net debt (~$5.8m) at H1-2026 from net cash ($0.7m) at FY25 due to continued cloud/technology investment; guidance signals a return toward cash generation in the second half

Longer-term aspiration versus FY25 actual ARR of $163.0m and H1-2026 ARR of $170.1m; contingent on continued Vista Cloud migration, Vista Payments scale-up and adjacency expansion (FECs, film distribution)
H1-2026 actual Vista Payments ARR surpassed $2m with 11 clients live; management cites implied gross transaction value potential of ~US$22bn at scale

items.target: Incremental cloud-acceleration costs fully recovered through increased free cash flow
items.notes: Management guidance framing the multi-year P&L drag from accelerated Vista Cloud onboarding (an extra $8.5m invested in FY25) as a temporary investment phase

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Stuart Dickinson said momentum in Vista Cloud 'continues to build' and that expanded delivery capacity is allowing the company to convert its cloud pipeline at pace, while Vista Payments has now been live long enough to demonstrate clear value for the company and its clients. Management expressed confidence in both industry outlook (citing a strong 2026 film slate and resilient/growing younger-audience engagement) and Vista's continued growth, while Chair Susan Peterson acknowledged 2025 was 'a challenging year for shareholder returns amid global volatility in software company valuations' but reaffirmed confidence in long-term value creation from cloud adoption, AI integration and Vista's global market-leading position.

bull_case: Dominant, defensible market position (~46-48% enterprise share) in a niche, mission-critical software vertical with high switching costs and limited credible full-scale competition

Accelerating SaaS/cloud transition (SaaS revenue +25% in FY25, +38% in H1-2026) is structurally improving revenue quality and margins, with EBITDA margin guided to 18-20% in FY26 versus 17.2% in FY25 and low-teens in 2023

Multiple large, high-profile new enterprise wins in 2026 (Cinepolis Mexico, Cineworld UK, Cinemex return, Kinepolis, ODEON/AMC expansion) demonstrate a strong and growing pipeline that outpaces delivery capacity

New revenue optionality from Vista Payments (embedded payments) and identified adjacencies (Family Entertainment Centres, film distribution) support the 2030 ARR aspiration of $315m, nearly double FY25's $163m
Governance overhang from the 2024-2025 Potentia/Admetus activist campaign has been resolved with their full exit, removing a source of distraction and share-register uncertainty

Secular tailwind from a resurgent global box office (up 12% in 2025, forecast to grow further in 2026) and reported strengthening engagement among younger/Gen Z moviegoers supports Vista's usage-linked revenue
bear_case: Profitability remains thin and volatile — FY25 NPAT of only $2.6m on $164.3m revenue, and H1-2026 posted a widened net loss of $1.5m alongside a swing into net debt (~$5.8m) from net cash, showing the cloud transition is still a multi-year cash cost before benefits are 'fully recovered' (not expected until end of 2030)
Cinema industry cyclicality and content-slate dependency mean a weak box-office year (as occurred around the 2023 writers'/actors' strikes) can directly hit revenue and client capex appetite

Small-cap NZX/ASX software valuation has been volatile and de-rated meaningfully (52-week range roughly NZ$1.56-$3.54), and management itself flagged 'global volatility in software company valuations' as a headwind to shareholder returns

Execution risk in scaling Vista Cloud onboarding — only 35% of sites had transitioned by FY25, and management acknowledges client demand is outpacing current delivery capacity, requiring continued hiring and cost investment with uncertain near-term payback

Governance concentration risk persists with a long-tenured, non-independent co-founder director (Murray Holdaway, ~22 years, ~2.4% holder) still on the board, and the 2024-2025 activist episode illustrates the company's exposure to future shareholder activism given its historically low profitability relative to revenue scale
